questions.q: A retention team wants a ranked call list of the riskiest customers once a month. Which serving design fits best?
options: A real-time API with a 50 ms latency target
A streaming pipeline scoring every click
A scheduled batch job that scores all customers and writes a file or table
No model at all
questions.explain: The score is not needed inside a live request and can be a day or month old, so a scheduled batch job is simpler and cheaper.

questions.q: Which situation most clearly REQUIRES real-time inference?
options: Scoring a whole customer table overnight
Producing a weekly report
Refreshing a dashboard once a day
Approving a card payment while the customer waits, using data that only exists at request time
questions.explain: When the decision happens inside a live request and key inputs exist only at that moment, batch precomputation cannot help.

questions.q: In the lesson's measurements, why was batch scoring so much cheaper per prediction?
options: Batch uses a different, simpler model
One vectorized call over many rows amortizes per-call overhead that single-row and HTTP calls pay every time
Batch skips preprocessing
The API was deliberately slowed down
questions.explain: Per-request overhead dominates real-time cost; scoring 100,000 rows in one call spreads that overhead across every row.

questions.q: Why should you treat the lesson's timing numbers (0.6 microseconds per row, 8.4 ms median) as illustrative only?
options: They came from one laptop, a small linear model, and a local network, so your results will differ
They were invented rather than measured
Timing measurements are never meaningful
Batch and real-time cannot be compared
questions.explain: The numbers were measured, but on specific hardware and a small model. The pattern generalizes; the exact values do not.

questions.q: What should every stored batch score row include, as in the lesson's job?
options: The customer's password
Only the probability
The model version and scoring date, so each score can be traced later
A copy of the training data
questions.explain: Recording version and date gives the same traceability as the API's model_version field and supports monitoring and audits.
